planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring and stake the leading shoot early if an upright weeping form is wanted; left unstaked it trails along the ground as a groundcover.

directions: Inversa is a classic weeping cultivar of Norway spruce whose pendulous side branches cascade from whatever leader is trained, so its ultimate shape depends entirely on staking: trained vertically it becomes a narrow weeping column, left alone it sprawls as an irregular groundcover mound. Plant in well-drained, average to moist soil in full sun for the densest branching, though it tolerates light shade. Little pruning is required beyond occasional removal of an overly dominant leader if a tidier silhouette is wanted. Its dramatic, sculptural habit makes it a long-lived specimen for rock gardens, terraced slopes, or as a trained accent near entries.

planting.note: Set out in spring with a stake to establish a straight central leader; the long pendulous side branches will drape downward as the plant gains height.

directions: Frohburg forms a straight, upright central trunk with long, cord-like side branches that drape straight down close to the stem, giving a distinctive tent- or skirt-like silhouette distinct from more sprawling weeping spruce selections. Grow in well-drained, average to moist soil in full sun; staking the leader when young helps establish height before the weeping habit takes over. Needs minimal pruning, mainly to remove competing leaders. Works well as a dramatic narrow accent in a border or foundation planting where its vertical, cascading form can be appreciated up close.

planting.note: Set container-grown plants out in spring in well-drained soil; this slow, dense selection needs no special siting beyond avoiding standing water.

directions: Pimoko is a dwarf, globose to broadly conical selection of Serbian spruce prized for its tight, dense branching and the two-toned needles typical of the species, dark green above with silvery undersides. Growth is extremely slow, making it suitable for rock gardens and small landscapes for many years before it needs more room. Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Serbian spruce tolerates urban pollution and a range of soil types better than most spruces. Needs essentially no pruning beyond removing the rare dead interior branch.

planting.note: Set container-grown plants out in spring in well-drained soil; established plants handle heat, wind, and alkaline soil better than most dwarf pines.

directions: Compact Gem is a slow-growing, densely rounded dwarf selection of Bosnian pine, holding short, stiff, dark green needles in tight tufts on a compact globe-shaped plant. It is notably tolerant of heat, wind, alkaline soil, and urban pollution compared with most other dwarf pines, making it a durable choice for exposed sites. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun and avoid heavy, poorly drained clay. Requires little to no pruning to maintain its naturally dense, rounded form.

planting.note: Stake a leader when young if more height is wanted; left unstaked the contorted, weeping branches sprawl along the ground in an irregular, twisting mound.

directions: Uncle Fogy is a quirky, irregularly weeping selection of jack pine with contorted, pendulous branches that twist and cascade rather than growing upright, giving every plant a distinct, sculptural shape. It tolerates poor, sandy, and infertile soils far better than most ornamental conifers, reflecting jack pine's native range on dry, rocky sites. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; it is extremely cold hardy and drought tolerant once established. Best used as a dramatic specimen where its tangled, twisting branch structure can be viewed in the round.

common_name: Filifera Nana Dwarf Thread-Branch Sawara Cypress

planting.note: Set container-grown plants out in spring in moist, well-drained soil; mulch to keep roots cool and evenly moist through the first season.

directions: Filifera Nana is a dwarf, mounding form of the thread-branch Sawara cypress, holding the same drooping, string-like sprays of foliage as the larger thread cypress but staying compact and dense for many years. Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, siting it with some afternoon shade in hot climates to prevent browning. Needs little pruning beyond removing the occasional dead interior branch. Its cascading, fine-textured foliage suits foundation plantings, rock gardens, and mixed conifer borders.

common_name: Minima Glauca Dwarf Blue Lawson Cypress

planting.note: Set container-grown plants out in spring in moist, well-drained soil away from drying winter winds, which can brown the foliage.

directions: Minima Glauca is a long-cultivated dwarf, globose selection of Lawson cypress, holding dense, tightly packed sprays of blue-gray-green foliage on a slow-growing rounded mound. Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, sheltering from harsh winter wind and intense afternoon sun to keep foliage from browning. Requires very little pruning given its naturally neat, rounded habit. Its small size and soft color make it well suited to rock gardens, trough plantings, and foundation beds.
